claims.natural_statement: The strongest old abstract claim C_CUT_ABSTRACT@2 asserts finite exhaustive cut-symbol surjections over every commutative Q-algebra, with coefficient generation proved internally and a Hilbert upper bound over characteristic-zero fields. This assertion is under substantive review; its BFN application is not included.

The archived C_CUT_CORE@2 Lean proof covers only universal positive-part excesses under the displayed disjointness hypotheses, orientation signs, finite sums/products, and finite-support cardinality. Matching historical compilation is not a formal proof of generation, trace cosets, Reynolds averaging or BFN geometry.

For the explicit unshifted free-module invariant algebra over any commutative Q-algebra in CTX_REVIEW_044, the all-data dressed cut-symbol surjections, internal coefficient generation, finite exhaustion and nonnegative shifts of old C_CUT_ABSTRACT@2 are supported by the prose proof. The BFN application C_CUT_SYMBOL@4 still requires INPUT_LAURENT. This is a human assessment, not new kernel evidence or independent acceptance.

The generation and coefficient-quotient implications of C_MINUSCULE@1-2 and C_COEFF_SURJ@1 are supported within their exact scope; the source proof of C_LAURENT@1 is conditional on the coefficient-, charge- and grading-compatible BFN minuscule/localization interface and is not certified by abstract generation.

The source argument for C_KERNEL@1 coherently gives ker(R to B_F) contained in ker(R to H_F^*(X)), hence a specified coefficient-compatible surjection, provided the stated BFN, finite correspondence, equivariant sheaf and Kirwan interfaces hold. No reverse inclusion or dimension equality follows from this unit.

The invariant reachability recurrence and its formal-series substitution into the ordinary Hausel formula in C_COUNTING@1 are supported under the stated equivariant Thom/Gysin and determinant moment-level comparison inputs, without replacing the cut ideal by its radical. This is distinct from the symbol-surjection theorem.

For C_LOOP_CASE@1, the specified graded coefficient-compatible surjection together with the cut-symbol upper bound and equal counting polynomial implies an isomorphism degree by degree. This is a conditional assembly, not independent evidence for its geometric inputs.

For C_DEFORM@1 and C_FULL_TORUS@1, the free-target flavor kernel argument, Weyl-norm unit calculation and homogeneous ideal descent are supported; the resulting full-torus comparison remains conditional on the stated BFN base-change, prequotient localization, stability and moment-map interfaces.

For C_POLY_MAPS@1, the retrieved polynomial Hall-generation and trigonometric operator theorems support the inputs, but the general repeated-slot filtered degeneration, lift independence and full loop/sign comparison are not independently established by the old artifacts. Parameter regularity is distinct from absence of gauge-root denominators.

For C_ROOT_CHARGE@1, C_ROOT_MOMENT@1 and C_COCHAR@1, the source root-support, moment-block and complementary-monopole argument is coherent conditional on the polynomial Hall bridge, BFN conventions and moment-map interfaces. The block needs a scalar stabilizer subgroup, not an exactly scalar stabilizer. Its conclusion concerns actual fixed-scheme ideals, including dimension-hyperplane characters.

C_HIKITA@1 follows formally and coefficientwise from the full-torus comparison and equality of cocharacter/full-charge ideals if all upstream interfaces hold with the same gradings. The local cut certificate alone does not independently establish the full theorem or the entire manuscript.

The review index accounts for all 18 inventory paths, all 28 versions of 22 historical claims, both contexts, eight routes, seventeen evidence records, and twenty-two graph nodes; nine substantive units each have a report and structured Engineer assessment. Nine snapshot-manifested paths and ten manuscript TeX entries were distinguished. Native independent review and the missing active proof-graph gate remain pending.
